## Server Installation & Branch Information

To install the Project Zomboid Dedicated Server via SteamCMD, run: `steamcmd +login anonymous +force_install_dir /pzserver +app_update 380870 validate +quit`, which installs the latest server (Build 41 by default).

### Beta Branch Options

The search results show information about different server branches:

- **Build 42 Unstable**: For Build 42 unstable, use the `-beta unstable` branch. The command is: `./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir ~/pzserver +login anonymous +app_update 380870 -beta unstable validate +quit`.

- **Build 41 Legacy**: If the branch still says `unstable` or `b41multiplayer`, delete the value to switch to the stable Build 42 branch.

- **Build 42 Stable**: Drop the `-beta` flag and you get 42.20 (the current stable version).

### Important Notes

Every player has to pick the same branch on their own copy of the game: right-click Project Zomboid in the Steam library, choose Properties, open Game Versions & Betas, and select the matching channel.

Build 42 unstable will likely receive frequent patches, and if you're running it, you must update the server whenever the game updates (or players won't be able to join due to version mismatch).

I've found comprehensive information about Project Zomboid dedicated server RAM requirements. Here are the key findings:

## RAM Requirements Formula

The sizing community has converged on roughly 6GB base plus 0.5GB per player, though there is no fixed "0.5 GB per player" rule in the game—heap demand depends on peak concurrent players, loaded chunks, zombie density, vehicles, mods, and uptime.

More specifically for baselines, Build 42 requires approximately 2.5–4.0 GB baseline for a quiet dedicated process, with about 0.15–0.35 GB of extra heap planning band per peak player.

## JVM Heap Settings (-Xmx)

Java's memory is bounded by the -Xmx maximum-heap setting, not by how much RAM the machine has. If you put PZ on a 16GB box but leave -Xmx at a low default, the server will fill that small heap and crash with an out-of-memory error while 12GB of system RAM sits unused.

The fix is to set -Xmx to match your sizing, in ProjectZomboid64.json or the launch options, leaving 1-2GB for the operating system. On a 16GB box dedicated to PZ, that means roughly -Xmx14g.

## Build 42 Considerations

For Build 42: 8GB minimum for a small group, 12-16GB for 8-16 players, and B42 is heavier across the board: basements, taller buildings, and the new crafting/animal systems all consume more memory.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about Project Zomboid's servertest_SandboxVars.lua settings:

## Overview

The servertest_SandboxVars.lua file allows you to adjust zombie population, loot rarity, XP multipliers, and other gameplay variables on your Project Zomboid server. Sandbox settings control the core gameplay experience on your server, including how many zombies spawn, how often loot respawns, how fast players gain XP, and other world simulation variables.

## Key Settings

**Zombie Population:**
The top-level Zombies field uses an inverted legacy scale where 1 = the most zombies and 5 = none. To control zombie population, set PopulationMultiplier (0–4, in the SandboxVars file) below 1.0.

**Zombie Speed:**
ZombieLore.Speed (Sprinters vs Fast Shamblers vs Shamblers) changes the entire tone of the game far more than any other single setting. To make zombies slower, set Speed to Shamblers (3).

**Loot Rarity:**
Loot rarity per category (Food, Weapon, Ammo, Medical, Mechanics…) uses a shared scale in servertest_SandboxVars.lua. Lower numbers = scarcer loot.

**Day Length & XP:**
Every gameplay knob (zombie population, loot multipliers, skill XP, day length, weather) is controlled in this file. To level faster, increase the XpMultiplier — it speeds up XP gain for all skills.

**Important Note:**
Changes take effect after a server restart. Stop the server before editing — PZ rewrites SandboxVars.lua on shutdown and will overwrite your changes if you edit while running.

content.text:
# Project Zomboid Dedicated Server — 2026 Research

## ⚠️ Current-status correction (verify this before building the wizard)
The brief's premise is now **out of date**. Build 42 multiplayer is no longer beta-only:
- **B42 multiplayer entered unstable** on **11 Dec 2025** (v42.13).
- **B42 went fully stable — multiplayer included — on 29 July 2026** (v42.20; current build 42.20.2 after two hotfixes). It is now the **default public branch**; you no longer need a beta flag to run a B42 MP server.
- One day after stable launch (30 July 2026) PZ hit an all-time peak of **79,670 concurrent players** — the game is at its most popular right now.
- **Build 41 is now the legacy branch**, offered via a named beta (`legacy41` / historically `b41multiplayer`). B41 and B42 saves/worlds are **not cross-compatible** — upgrading requires a fresh world.

Sources: [pinehosting — B42 now stable](https://pinehosting.com/blog/project-zomboid-build-42-is-now-stable-everything-new-in-42-20/), [doomhosting — B42 stable 29 Jul 2026](https://www.doomhosting.com/blog/project-zomboid-build-42-stable-release-july-29-2026), [shockbyte — B42 MP release](https://shockbyte.com/blog/project-zomboid-build-42-multiplayer)

---

## Self-hostable?
**Yes.** The Indie Stone ships an official, free, standalone **Project Zomboid Dedicated Server** as a separate SteamCMD app. It requires no game purchase and installs via anonymous login. Officially supports **up to 32 players**. Sources: [SteamDB app 380870](https://steamdb.info/app/380870/), [pimylifeup](https://pimylifeup.com/project-zomboid-dedicated-server-linux/)

## SteamCMD app ID & install
- **Dedicated server app ID: `380870`** (the base game is `108600` — do not confuse them). Confirmed across 3+ sources incl. SteamDB. [SteamDB 380870](https://steamdb.info/app/380870/), [shattered.io](https://shattered.io/project-zomboid-dedicated-server/)
- **Install / update (Linux):**
  ```
  steamcmd +force_install_dir /pzserver +login anonymous +app_update 380870 validate +quit
  ```
- **Start scripts:** `start-server.sh` (Linux) / `StartServer64.bat` (Windows 64-bit). JVM args live in `ProjectZomboid64.json`.
- **First-run `-adminpassword` requirement:** On first launch the server creates the `admin` account and **prompts for an admin password interactively**. For unattended/automated provisioning you must pass it non-interactively:
  ```
  ./start-server.sh -adminpassword <PASS> -servername servertest
  ```
  This is a common headless-provisioning gotcha — without it, first boot blocks on a stdin prompt. [pimylifeup](https://pimylifeup.com/project-zomboid-dedicated-server-linux/)
- **Ports:** `16261/UDP` (DefaultPort) + `16262` (DefaultPort+1, auto). Add RCON `27015/TCP` if enabled.

## Editions / versions / branches (SteamCMD betas)
Same app ID `380870`, branch selected via `-beta`:
| Offer | SteamCMD flag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **B42 stable (recommended default)** | *(no `-beta`)* — default public branch | v42.20+, MP shipped, most players are here |
| **B41 stable MP (legacy option)** | `-beta legacy41` (formerly `-beta b41multiplayer`) | For established B41 communities/mod stability |
| **B42 unstable** | `-beta unstable` | Frequent patches; server must update in lockstep with clients or version mismatch blocks joins |

**Recommendation for the wizard:** as of Aug 2026, default to **B42 stable (no beta flag)** and offer **B41 (`legacy41`)** as the "legacy / max mod compatibility" alternative. This *inverts* the original brief (which assumed B41 was the only viable MP branch). Critically, **every player must select the matching branch** in Steam (Properties → Betas) or they can't connect. [doomhosting — switch branch](https://www.doomhosting.com/help/articles/how-to-switch-to-project-zomboid-build-42-server), [gamers.wiki — B42 split](https://gamers.wiki/en/games/project-zomboid/guides/project-zomboid-servers-and-mods-after-the-build-42-split)

## Mods ecosystem
- **Platform: Steam Workshop.** Mods are grouped via **Workshop Collections**, which map cleanly to a "1-click modpack" wizard feature.
- **The classic two-line gotcha:** the server config needs **BOTH** lines, and they take **different kinds of ID**:
  - `WorkshopItems=` → **numeric Workshop IDs** (from the mod's URL). Tells the server what to *download*.
  - `Mods=` → **internal string Mod IDs** (baked in the mod, not the display name). Tells the server what to *activate/load*.
  - Both are semicolon-separated. If you fill only `WorkshopItems`, the mod downloads but never loads; wrong/missing `Mods` IDs silently disable it. **Load order in `Mods=` matters** for dependencies. Example:
    ```
    WorkshopItems=1234567890;987654321
    Mods=BritasWeaponPack;Hydrocraft
    ```
  [xgamingserver — mods](https://xgamingserver.com/blog/how-to-install-steam-workshop-mods-to-your-project-zomboid-server/), [pinehosting — add mods](https://pinehosting.com/blog/how-to-add-mods-to-your-project-zomboid-server-a-step-by-step-guide/)
- **Popular mods to seed a modpack picker:** Brita's Weapon Pack, Brita's Armor Pack, Superb Survivors (NPCs, largely B41), Common Sense, Autotsar Trailers, Mod Manager, Change Sandbox Options, Filibuster Rhymes' Used Cars, True Music. (Note: many big B41 mods still have partial/no B42 ports — relevant to the branch choice.)

## Key config files
Server profile is named `servertest` by default (the `-servername` value prefixes all files):
1. **`servertest.ini`** — main server + gameplay-lite settings.
2. **`servertest_SandboxVars.lua`** — the sandbox/world simulation knobs.
3. **`servertest.db`** — SQLite player/whitelist DB (bans, accounts, coords).
   > Split matters: connection/moderation/mod settings live in **`.ini`**; world-feel settings (zombies, loot, XP) live in **`SandboxVars.lua`**. PZ **rewrites `SandboxVars.lua` on shutdown**, so edit only while the server is stopped or edits are lost.

**12–15 most-tuned settings:**

*In `servertest.ini`:*
- `PublicName` — server browser name
- `Password` — join password
- `Open` — allow open joining vs whitelist-only
- `MaxPlayers` — cap (default up to 32)
- `PVP` — enable/disable player-vs-player
- `PauseEmpty` (PauseAllVehiclesWhenEmpty/PauseEmpty) — pause time when no players online
- `GlobalChat` — global chat toggle
- `Mods=` / `WorkshopItems=` — the two mod lines above
- `SpawnPoint` / spawn region settings + `SpawnItems` (starting gear)
- `DefaultPort` (16261), `RCONPort`/`RCONPassword`

*In `servertest_SandboxVars.lua`:*
- **Zombie `PopulationMultiplier`** (0–4; the top-level `Zombies` field uses an inverted 1=most…5=none legacy scale)
- **`ZombieLore.Speed`** (Sprinters / Fast Shamblers / Shamblers), plus **Strength** and **Toughness**
- **Loot rarity** per category (Food/Weapon/Ammo/Medical/Mechanics — lower = scarcer)
- **`DayLength`** (in-game day duration)
- **`XpMultiplier`** (global skill XP rate)

Sources: [xgamingserver — servertest.ini](https://xgamingserver.com/blog/servertest-ini-project-zomboid-server-explained/), [respawnhost — sandbox settings](https://respawnhost.com/en/wiki/games/project-zomboid/project-zomboid-sandbox-settings/), [hosthavoc — sandbox](https://hosthavoc.com/wiki/game-servers/project-zomboid/sandbox-settings)

## Resource baseline (RAM / CPU)
- **RAM is bounded by JVM `-Xmx`, not machine RAM** — set it in `ProjectZomboid64.json` (or launch opts). A big box with a low `-Xmx` will OOM-crash while system RAM sits idle. Leave 1–2 GB for the OS (e.g. `-Xmx14g` on a 16 GB box).
- **Cited sizing:**
  - **B41:** ~2 GB base + ~few hundred MB/player.
  - **B42 (heavier):** ~**2.5–4.0 GB baseline** for an idle process + **~0.15–0.35 GB extra heap per peak player**. Community rule-of-thumb converges near **~6 GB base + ~0.5 GB/player**, but real demand scales with zombie density, loaded chunks, vehicles, mods, and uptime.
- **CPU:** PZ multiplayer is largely **single-thread-bound for the main sim loop** — high per-core clock beats core count.

**Suggested product tiers:**
| Tier | Players | RAM (`-Xmx`) |
|---|---|---|
| Small / friends | 2–4 | 6–8 GB |
| Standard | 8 | 8–12 GB |
| Large community | 12–16 | 12–16 GB |
| Heavy-mod / 24+ | 24–32 | 16–24 GB+ |

Sources: [dedicatedgameservers.net — B42 RAM reality](https://dedicatedgameservers.net/articles/project-zomboid-dedicated-server-requirements-2026/), [pzfans — memory per player count](https://pzfans.com/how-much-server-memory-is-needed-for-different-player-counts/), [supercraft.host — allocate RAM](https://supercraft.host/wiki/project-zomboid/allocate_ram/)

## Hosting demand signal
**High and currently peaking.** PZ is one of the most consistently self-/rented-hosted survival games, and the July 2026 B42 stable launch drove an all-time concurrency record (~79.7k). Every major game-host (Shockbyte, Host Havoc, Pingperfect, GTXGaming, XGamingServer, plus a large DIY/Docker community) offers PZ, and the B41→B42 split is generating fresh setup/migration demand. Strong, active market to enter.

## Verdict

**Recommended default config:**
- Branch: **B42 stable** (no `-beta`; current player majority). Offer **B41 `legacy41`** as a labeled legacy/mod-compat alternative.
- App `380870`, anonymous SteamCMD install with `validate`.
- Auto-generate `-adminpassword` at provision time (never block on the stdin prompt).
- MaxPlayers 8, PVP off, PauseEmpty on, GlobalChat on, whitelist off (Open=true) with a password by default.
- Sensible `-Xmx` bound to the chosen tier, leaving 1–2 GB for OS.

**Highest-value wizard options (3–5):**
1. **Branch selector** — B42 stable (default) vs B41 legacy, with a clear warning that clients must match the branch.
2. **Player-count / RAM tier** — drives `MaxPlayers` and auto-sets `-Xmx` from the tier table.
3. **Difficulty preset → SandboxVars** — one control that writes zombie population multiplier, speed (Shamblers/Sprinters), loot rarity, and XP multiplier (e.g. Relaxed / Survivor / Apocalypse).
4. **Steam Workshop modpack installer** — paste a Workshop **Collection** URL and auto-populate **both** `WorkshopItems` and `Mods` (solving the two-line gotcha for the user).
5. **PVP + password/whitelist toggle** — public-open vs private-passworded server in one switch.

---

Sources: [SteamDB 380870](https://steamdb.info/app/380870/) · [pinehosting B42 stable](https://pinehosting.com/blog/project-zomboid-build-42-is-now-stable-everything-new-in-42-20/) · [doomhosting branch switch](https://www.doomhosting.com/help/articles/how-to-switch-to-project-zomboid-build-42-server) · [xgamingserver mods](https://xgamingserver.com/blog/how-to-install-steam-workshop-mods-to-your-project-zomboid-server/) · [dedicatedgameservers.net RAM](https://dedicatedgameservers.net/articles/project-zomboid-dedicated-server-requirements-2026/) · [respawnhost sandbox](https://respawnhost.com/en/wiki/games/project-zomboid/project-zomboid-sandbox-settings/) · [pimylifeup Linux setup](https://pimylifeup.com/project-zomboid-dedicated-server-linux/)
